report.summary: The checkout service is down because the checkout Deployment in namespace astronomy-shop has a pod-template nodeSelector of kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node, and no node in the cluster carries that hostname. The template change forced a rollout at 10:04:23 (and a second ReplicaSet at 10:04:29) that killed the previously running checkout pod checkout-6c769b88b5-lw6bx; both replacement pods (checkout-54579c864c-vw94b, checkout-c69887c97-6lpd2) are Pending/Unschedulable with the scheduler message "0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane}, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector", and the checkout Service's Endpoints object has no subsets. Checkout was still serving successfully at 10:04:17 (PlaceOrder, rpc.grpc.status_code=0, 45.2 ms) and the load generator reported fail_ratio 0.0 at 10:04:29; from 10:04:23 onward its POST /api/checkout requests hang for 15 s and frontend-proxy returns HTTP 504, which the locust fetcher records at 10:04:39 as "504 Server Error: Gateway Timeout for url: /api/checkout". All 22 other astronomy-shop Deployments report one available replica, and every sampled pod has 0 container restarts; no networkpolicies, resourcequotas or mutating webhooks exist in the namespace, and no ConfigMap mentions extra-node. Observed impact of this cause is limited to checkout availability, 15 s /api/checkout latency in frontend, 504 errors in frontend-proxy, and 504 failures in load-generator; earlier connection-refused/503/500 errors between 10:03:44 and 10:04:19 are startup transients that precede the checkout rollout.

Whether a node named/labelled extra-node existed earlier in the window and was removed cannot be determined, because node objects reflect only their state at query time.

next_steps: Consult the cluster audit log or the change-history source for the actor and patch that added nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node to the checkout Deployment around 2026-11-24T10:04:23Z.

Remove the unsatisfiable nodeSelector from the checkout Deployment (or make a node with kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node exist) and verify pods schedule and the checkout Endpoints object is populated.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
